title: 新年大計同朋友傾

sourceNotes: The verb 諗 (nam2) means "to think" in Cantonese and is more colloquial than 想 (soeng2), though both are used. 諗 specifically means "to think about/consider" while 想 can mean both "to think" and "to want." The pattern 有冇 (jau5 mou5) is the question form asking "have or not have": 你有冇諗 (nei5 jau5 mou5 nam2) = "have you thought about...?" This is the standard A-not-A question structure. 邊隻 (bin1 zek3) uses the classifier 隻 (zek3) for languages in Cantonese, which differs from Mandarin. This is the correct classifier for languages in Hong Kong Cantonese. 點樣 (dim2 joeng2) asks "how/in what way" and is composed of 點 (dim2) "how" + 樣 (joeng2) "manner." Itʼs the standard way to ask about methods. The emphatic pattern 一定得 (jat1 ding6 dak1) means "definitely can/will succeed" and is commonly used for encouragement. 得 (dak1) here means "can/be able to." 乜都 (mat1 dou1) means "anything/everything" and combines the question word 乜 (mat1) "what" with 都 (dou1) "all" to create an indefinite pronoun. Confidence Level: High
